text.p: The Turkish lira closed weaker at 90,110 to the dollar on Wednesday after 89,830 on Tuesday on banks' dollar demand despite ongoing cash squeeze.
Bankers said expectations of higher inflation in the last quarter fuelled demand for the U.S. currency.
The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory monthly hard currency transfers at 89,850 lira, up from 89,675 at yesterday's close.
Bankers said cash demand remained strong as banks paid 114 trillion lira to the Treasury for Tuesday's 189-day t-bill auction in return for 79.6 trillion lira of maturing t-bills.
Central bank injected a total of 71.7 trillion lira to the market to relieve the liquidity shortage.
It funded 28.9 trillion lira by buying five-day repos from banks at an average annual rate of 74.39 percent on the open market.

The bank also funded 42.8 trillion lira overnight cash at 75 percent on the interbank. Overnight rates brushed a low of 74 percent in the day. Central bank's overnight lending was 42.2 trillion on Tuesday.
In the t-bill market, yields firmed by between one-two points on tight liquidity
The yield on the most active March 26, 1997 paper, sold at an average rate of 125.64 percent at yesterday's auction, firmed to 127.05 percent.
The second most heavily traded December 25 paper firmed to 112.25 percent from 111.21 percent Tuesday average.
